mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 anticipates higher future discount rates, leading to negative 20-day forward returns as present value of expected cash flows falls.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: In at least 60% of FEDFUNDS up moves >0.25pp, the 20-day SPX forward return is non-negative, or the IC is above 0.05 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) for two consecutive months predicts a disinflationary environment that reduces equity risk premia, resulting in positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 20 rolling window tests, the 60-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05), or inflation recovers before the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market tightness) above the 50th percentile of the past 12 months coincides with rising wage growth expectations, pushing 20-day SPX returns to the positive via higher consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 50th percentile of the past 12 months
failure_condition: In 40% of PAYEMS tightness up moves past the 50th percentile, the 20-day forward return is negative or the IC is below -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in GDPC1 (real private demand) of at least 3% signal a strengthening economy, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by at least 3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 70% of GDPC1 >3% monthly up moves, the 5-day forward return is not positive (IC < 0.02).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (supplied output) of over 2% in a month indicates supply-side weakness that raises uncertainty and drives negative 20-day SPX forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >2% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 30 such INDPRO drops, the 20-day return is not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both GDPC1 (demand) and HOUST (industrial production) above their 75th percentile for the past 6 months creates a dual-recovery signal that drives positive 60-day SPX forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 75th percentile and HOUST > 75th percentile for past 6 months
failure_condition: Interaction IC < 0.1 over the 60-day horizon, or 60-day return not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the expectation of lower future labor costs supports corporate cost-cutting and positive 20-day SPX returns.
failure_condition: In 50% of UNRATE <4% triple-move windows, the 20-day forward return is non-positive (IC >= 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to FEDFUNDS > 4% indicates aggressive policy tightening that raises real discount rates, producing negative 5-day SPX forward returns regardless of other macro variables.
failure_condition: Over 40% of days with FEDFUNDS >4%, the 5-day forward return is non-negative (IC > 0.04).
